items.title: India Glycols shares rebound 11.6% after 5-day losing run, up 1530% from 2020 lows. Should investors buy, sell or hold?
points: After being stuck in losses for five consecutive trading sessions, shares of India Glycols, a specialty chemicals maker, staged a strong rebound in Monday's trade, recovering 11.6% to ₹295 apiece and erasing most of their recent losses.
Around 15.5 million shares changed hands across the BSE and NSE, nearly 39 times the stock's weekly average trading volume, according to Trendlyne data.
Despite Monday's recovery, the stock remains down 11% in November so far.
From its 2020 lows, the stock has surged nearly 1,530% as of Monday's close.

items.title: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre warns of possible misuse of WhatsApp Web sessions
points: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre suggested using the incognito and private browsing mode when use is unavoidable.

File. | Photo Credit: Reuters The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs, has warned WhatsApp users about the possible misuse of authenticated web sessions to gain unauthorised access to their accounts.
The unit has asked users to exercise caution while accessing WhatsApp Web, particularly on office computers, shared systems, public computers and devices that may be accessible to others.
It recommended users to avoid exchanging government-related, organisational, financial, confidential or other sensitive information through WhatsApp Web mode on computers.
Users have also been advised against keeping their accounts permanently logged in and to manually log out after every session.
Where using WhatsApp Web was unavoidable, the users were advised to opt for ‘Incognito’ or ‘Private Browsing’ mode on trusted computers and log out manually before closing the browser.
The unit also urged WhatsApp users to remain alert to unusual account activity.

items.title: Two killed, 13 injured as bus hits van near Mailam
points: Two persons, including an Ayyappa devotee, were killed and 13 others sustained injuries when a private bus crashed into a parked van carrying Sabarimala pilgrims on the Chennai-Tiruchi National Highway at Kannigapuram near Mailam on Monday (November 23, 2026).
The deceased were identified as Jana alias Rajendran, 24, the van driver, and C.

The bus then struck the van carrying Sabarimala pilgrims before crashing into a roadside eatery.

items.title: PM Modi, Balen Shah inaugurate 100-metre motor bridge linking Uttarakhand with Nepal
points: A 110-metre motor bridge connecting India and Nepal at Chharchhum near Dharchula, over the Kali River in Uttarakhand’s Pithoragarh district, was virtually inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah from New Delhi…

In a joint press statement with Shah, Modi said the Dharchula road bridge between Uttarakhand and Nepal had been inaugurated and the foundation stone for an integrated check post at Banbasa had also been laid.
Chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said the inauguration of the Chharchhum motor bridge would give a “fresh impetus to India-Nepal ties and the development of border regions”.
Recalling that he had laid the foundation stone for the bridge on September 19, 2022, Dhami described its inauguration as a matter of joy and pride for residents of the border region.
The bridge is the second motorable bridge along the India-Nepal border in Uttarakhand, with the other one located at Banbasa in Champawat district.
Construction of the Chharchhum bridge began in 2022, with its foundation stone laid by Dhami.

items.title: Karthigai Deepam festival tomorrow, century-old dispute over stone pillar 'deepathoon' returns to spotlight in Tamil Nadu
points: Karthigai Deepam festival on November 24 will see a ceremonial lamp lit at a disputed stone pillar, or the deepathoon, atop Thirupparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai district, following an interim order by the Supreme Court.
In its ruling on November 20, the court permitted the ritual as a one-time exception, restricting its conduct to individuals authorised by the Subramanian Swamy temple and government officials.
The Arulmigu Subramanian Swamy Temple Devasthana filed a civil suit in 1920, claiming title over the entire hill.
The matter was addressed again in 1996, when the high court ordered that the Karthigai Deepam should be lit at an alternative location on the hill's lower slopes, close to the Uchipillaiyar Temple.
The Tamil Nadu government has moved the Supreme Court seeking a review of its November 20 interim order.
CM Vijay-led Tamil Nadu government maintains that lighting the Karthigai Deepam at the stone pillar is not a customary or historically established temple practice.

items.title: Precious Shipping secures year-long ultramax charter
points: Thailand’s Precious Shipping has secured another index-linked ultramax charter with Singapore’s PACC Line, fixing the 2015-built Sarita Naree for up to 13 months at a current equivalent rate of around $23,700 per day.

The Khalid Hashim-led owner said the 62,964 dwt vessel started an 11-to-13-month charter on November 22 at a gross variable rate equivalent to 103% of the Baltic Exchange Supramax Index (BSI-63K) weighted time-charter average over the preceding 15 days.
The hire will fluctuate with the index rather than remain fixed at the current level.

The latest agreement follows a similar fixture in September, when Precious chartered its 2016-built ultramax Sunisa Naree to PACC Line for 11 to 13 months at the same 103% index-linked rate, then equivalent to about $23,000 per day.
Both vessels were built at China’s Taizhou Sanfu Ship Engineering, a yard that has become central to Precious Shipping’s fleet renewal programme.

items.title: Kansai Electric takes 40% stake in Polish offshore wind project
points: Japan’s Kansai Electric Power has agreed to acquire a 40% interest in Ocean Winds’ 390 MW BC-Wind offshore wind development in Poland, marking its first investment in the country.
The Japanese utility signed a share purchase agreement with Ocean Winds on November 19, and the transaction will be carried out through its wholly owned subsidiary, KPIC Netherlands.
Kansai will acquire its interest in C-Wind Polska, the project company developing the wind farm, leaving Ocean Winds with a 60% holding following completion.
BC-Wind is located approximately 23 km off Poland’s Baltic Sea coast and will comprise 26 Siemens Gamesa turbines with a maximum output of 15 MW each.
The project is expected to start generating electricity in 2028 and can supply around 500,000 Polish households.
Ocean Winds, a joint venture between EDP Renewables and Engie, reached financial close on BC-Wind in December 2025, securing approximately €2bn ($2.2bn) in project financing.

items.title: Street plays to promote co-existence between humans and wildlife organised in Kotagiri
points: The street plays were organised by Keystone Foundation in collaboration with the Forest Department.

The two-day human-wildlife interaction awareness programme included street plays performed by Aayudham Foundation, Coimbatore, which ‘presented a series of engaging street plays to raise awareness among local communities about reducing negative…

The performances focused on the importance of peaceful coexistence with wildlife, particularly species such as sloth bears, leopards, tigers and elephants and practices that can be adopted by human communities to minimise negative interactions with wildlife.

Key themes of the plays included understanding wildlife behaviour, avoiding encounters with wild animals, responsible waste disposal and the role of improper waste management in attracting wildlife towards human settlements.
Through interactive and culturally engaging performances, the street plays highlighted how everyday human activities can influence wildlife movement and contribute to human–wildlife conflict.
The programme also encouraged villagers to adopt responsible practices, remain alert and work collectively towards creating safer environments for both people and wildlife, the release added.

items.title: Dhanraj murder case: Court convicts three accused, acquits 17 others
points: The Taliparamba Additional Sessions Court has convicted the first three accused in the murder of CPI(M) worker C.V.
Dhanraj, while acquitting the remaining 17 accused, giving them the benefit of the doubt.
The accused from fourth to the twentieth were acquitted by the court.
Dhanraj, a former CPI(M) branch secretary in Ezhimala and DYFI leader was hacked to death on the night of July 11, 2016.
The attack took place in front of his mother and wife at his residence in Kunnaru Karanthat, Ramanthali.
The testimony of Dhanraj’s mother proved crucial in the case.
The court acquitted accused Nos. 4 to 20 because it found the testimony of the first prosecution witness, Prajeesh, unreliable.
Pointing to a photograph of Dhanraj lying injured, the judge noted that he had suffered 37 cuts.

items.title: Karnataka Ministers, MLAs should stay in farmers’ homes during Belagavi legislature session to cut costs: Farmers’ outfit

Shivakumar, the presiding officers of the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council, and the leaders of the Congress, BJP and JD(S) legislature parties.

Mr. Shanthakumar has suggested that Ministers, MLAs and officials stay in farmers’ homes instead of hotels during the session, citing the financial constraints faced by the State Government in implementing its welfare schemes.
He said farmers were concerned about the State government’s financial position, particularly as it was convening a special session of the Legislature against the backdrop of the prevailing drought.

Pointing out that the government spends substantial amounts on hotel accommodation and other facilities for legislators and officials during every session, Mr. Shanthakumar appealed for a reduction in such expenditure.

Staying in farmers’ homes would also enable legislators to understand their problems first-hand and facilitate meaningful discussions during the Assembly session, paving the way for appropriate solutions,” he said.

points: Hyderabad Police have intensified security crowded public places, including railway stations, hotels, bus terminals and religious places.

The investigators are examining the email and associated digital information to establish the sender’s identity and verify the authenticity of the threat.

items.title: Karnataka Congress MLAs oppose elephant relocation; Motamma submits resignation
points: Congress MLA Nayana Motamma on Monday resigned from the Karnataka assembly in protest against the Forest Department’s operation to drive wild elephants from Belur in Hassan district towards Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary in Chikkamagaluru.
Her resignation came a day after she, along with two other Congress MLAs, threatened to quit if the operation was not stopped.
Motamma, who represents Mudigere, submitted her resignation at Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru and left without speaking to reporters.
Motamma, Sringeri MLA TD Rajegowda and Chikkamagaluru MLA HD Thammaiah have argued that bringing elephants from Hassan would worsen human-elephant conflict in their constituencies.
In comparison, Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary has about 141,000 acres of forest, with its buffer zone taking the total area to approximately 262,000 acres, he said.

items.title: Ecostani: No climate deal at Antalya will not derail renewable transition
points: In 2009, the COP at Copenhagen failed to reach an agreement.

In 2009, the renewable energy journey was just starting to have an impact on economies, with a major push from the European Union and then US president Barack Obama.

items.title: Jinhui finds new buyer for supramax at higher price
points: Hong Kong-based dry bulk owner Jinhui Shipping and Transportation has found a new buyer for its 2012-built supramax Jin Bi, securing $17.8m for a vessel it unsuccessfully tried to sell for $14.4m earlier this year.

points: In an advisory dated November 18, I4C said such unauthorised access could be exploited for fraud, phishing, social engineering or other malicious activities.

items.title: 'Unable to digest': BJP takes jibe at Rahul Gandhi after India ranks 3rd on Asia Power Index
points: Australian think tank Lowy Institute released its Asia Power Index Ranking for 2026, where India retained its "major power" status in Asia and increased its overall score to 40.5, despite a dip in economic capability.
The report also noted that India stood strong in the diplomatic field, making Prime Minister Narendra Modi Asia's second-most effective leader behind Xi Jinping.

Taking to X, BJP leader Sambit Patra said the report reflected India's progress in diplomatic influence, future resources, economic relationships, and defence networks, adding that the country was establishing its identity as a global power.

While addressing a rally in Telangana, BJP national president Nitin Nabin also attacked Rahul Gandhi over the latter's remarks on the Indian economy, saying the country was advancing significantly even by global standards.
BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad accused Gandhi of spreading falsehoods about India on foreign soil and ignoring the country's achievements on the global stage.

items.title: Kannur court convicts three RSS activists in murder of CPI(M) worker stabbed 37 times
points: Judge KN Prasanth of the Taliparamba Additional District Sessions Court found TP Biju, M Vipin and M Vaisakh, all RSS activists, guilty of direct involvement in the murder.
C Biju, one of the accused, was killed during the course of the trial in what was seen as a case of retaliatory murder by alleged CPI(M) workers.
Prosecution lawyer CK Sreedharan said that while the conviction of the first three accused was welcome, the acquittal of others would be challenged in a higher court.
“The accused 1 to 3 were directly involved in the murder as pointed out in our chargesheet.
They inflicted 37 stab wounds on the body of Dhanaraj.

items.title: Apple Reportedly Lines Up iPhone 18e, iPhone 18 and MacBook Neo 2 for Early 2027
points: Apple usually hides its launch calendars well, but 2027 seems to be an exception.
This is probably the first time we have a good idea of when (and which) the new Apple products will arrive in 2027, as multiple sources point to a similar schedule.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, one of the most reliable sources on everything Apple, says the company is gearing up to unveil cheaper hardware (the baseline variants) across all lineups between February and March 2027.
That’s also when Apple plans to unveil iOS 27.4.
Along with this, Apple could also unveil the baseline iPad 12, MacBook Neo (2nd Gen), and MacBook Air (M6).

The iPad could come with a new chipset (the A19 with Apple Intelligence and N1 chip), the MacBook Neo (with A19 Pro chip for more processing power), and a new MacBook Air in the classic Apple “chip-and-connectivity” fashion.

items.title: BIMCO-initiated proposal for an ISO methodology on shipbuilding emissions enters the ISO process
points: A proposed ISO Technical Specification would set a common way to calculate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from building a ship.
A proposal for a new ISO project has been submitted to the International Organization for Standardization (ISO).
The project would develop a common methodology for calculating GHG emissions from shipbuilding.
Danish Standards formally submitted it on 4 October 2026.
Participating national standards bodies are now voting on it, and the ballot closes on 27 December 2026.
If the proposal is approved, Everllence and Danish Standards will lead further development, with support from BIMCO.
From raw materials to sea trials The proposed Technical Specification covers cradle-to-gate emissions.
Practical calculation options The proposed methodology builds on the ISO 14040 and ISO 14060 families of standards and the GHG Protocol.

items.title: LNG Market Remained Under Pressure Last Week, As LPGs Firmed
points: The LNG market remained under pressure this week, with an abundance of prompt vessel availability in the Atlantic continuing to weigh on freight rates.
On the BLNG1 Gladstone–Tokyo route, rates declined $2,800 week-on-week to settle at $50,600/day.
The BLNG2 Sabine–Isle of Grain route fell $8,900 to settle at $20,800/day, with the Atlantic remaining considerably oversupplied amid limited arbitrage opportunities and increased FOB cargo sales.
Similarly, the BLNG3 Sabine–Tokyo route declined $15,200 to close at $40,400/day, reflecting the continued weakness in the Atlantic and reduced demand for longer-haul voyages.
Period rates also softened, with the six-month assessment falling $1,900 to $42,300/day, the one-year assessment down $2,267 to $50,633/day, and the three-year assessment easing $700 to $70,300/day.
On the BLPG1 Ras Tanura–Chiba route, rates settled at $252.40/tonne, with TCE earnings closing at $246,826/day.
The BLPG2 Houston–Flushing route softened marginally, declining $0.67 week-on-week to settle at $173.83/tonne, with TCE earnings down $479 to $204,608/day.

points: Hong Kong has formed an industry group to develop a green marine fuel trading platform and to explore a transaction-based price index, while the government expects lawmakers to pass a tax-break bill covering physical fuel trades on Nov.
25, officials said during Hong Kong Maritime Week 2026.
The platform would connect fuel suppliers in mainland China and overseas with buyers in the global shipping industry, Hong Kong’s Transport and Logistics Bureau said Nov.

items.title: Iran asserts control over Hormuz as strikes on Bahrain, Saudi Arabia escalate
points: Iran asserted control over the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday after claiming strikes on U.S. air defense radars in Bahrain, as renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia threatened to widen the regional conflict.
Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said Tehran, rather than foreign forces, controlled the strategic waterway, an obstacle to negotiations to end the war.
Washington maintains a maritime blockade against Iran and says American vessels are escorting commercial shipping through the strait.
Tehran insists ships must negotiate passage with Iranian authorities.

The latest confrontation followed claims by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps that it attacked two Patriot air defense radars at the al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain using missiles and drones.
The Guards described the operation as retaliation for alleged U.S. airspace violations and an attack on an Iranian radar installation on Hengam Island.
In Saudi Arabia, a Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at the kingdom’s western region.

items.title: WRI STATEMENT: Hollow Outcome at COP31 a Failure of Political Leadership
points: The UN’s COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkiye, ended without reaching agreement after more than two weeks of negotiations that stretched into overtime longer than ever before.
Countries became deadlocked over whether the cover decision would reiterate the call to transition away from fossil fuels and concerns that it promoted overreliance on carbon capture and storage.
Since consensus was not reached, the draft Antalya pact—along with its many elements—has no formal standing.
Ani Dasguputa, President and CEO, World Resources Institute said the following: “The hollow outcome at COP31 was a failure of political leadership, not a failure of the Paris Agreement.
“With it now inevitable that warming will exceed 1.5°C, people on the frontlines of the climate crisis cannot afford for governments to spend more than two weeks with almost nothing to show for it.
“The COP31 Presidency’s push to accelerate electrification by 35%, despite securing backing from more than 70 countries, was marred by its exclusion from a negotiated outcome like everything else.

items.title: Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say
points: An explosion on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base port was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya’s eastern government has said.
The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libyan state media reported, citing the eastern government.

Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC, reviewed by BBC Verify, shows a boat on fire at 0547 GMT at the Benghazi port, with a separate image captured several hours later appearing to show the same vessel partially submerged.
The eastern-based Government of National Stability (GNS) said the Russian ship was using the Benghazi port within the framework of an existing maritime agreement.
Sunday’s incident is under investigation, and authorities are coordinating with their Russian counterparts to determine the source of the suspected attack and who is responsible for it, GNS added.

items.title: Hanwha Ocean wins tanker order at highest price since 2008 crisis
points: Hanwha Ocean recently won a $272 million order for two very large crude carriers (VLCCs).
The price of $136 million per vessel is the highest since the 2008 global financial crisis.

Hanwha Ocean won an order on the 18th for two VLCCs with a capacity of 320,000 deadweight tons (DWT) each at a price of $136 million, or about 182.1 billion won, per vessel, according to the shipbuilding industry on the 20th.

Hanwha Ocean secured the latest contract at about $6.3 million more per vessel than it received for two VLCCs of the same size ordered by the same operator in April last year, when the price was $129.7 million per vessel.
The order price rose from $130.96 million per vessel in July to $133.5 million at the end of last month, before climbing to $136 million this month.

items.title: ARA fuel oil stocks rise 10% in November so far
points: The ARA’s independently held fuel oil stocks have averaged 10% higher in November so far, compared to October’s monthly average, according to Insights Global data.
Changes in monthly average ARA stocks from October to November (so far): Fuel oil stocks have risen by 70% from May, when they hit their lowest level in more than a decade.
However, inventories are still 5% below February levels, before Israel and the US went to war with Iran.
The ARA hub has imported 167,000 b/d of fuel oil so far in November, down from October’s 183,000 b/d, according to Vortexa cargo flows data.
The largest volumes have come from Mexico (21%), France (14%) and Venezuela (13%).
Most of it has gone to the UK (45%), Spain (21%) and Mauritania (10%).
The region’s independent gasoil inventories – which include diesel and heating oil – have gained 1% so far in November, compared to October, according to the Insights Global data.

items.title: Oil flows through Middle East chokepoints increased in the third quarter
points: Collective oil shipments through key chokepoints around the Middle East increased by 19% in the third quarter of 2026 (3Q26), according to our recently published Global Energy Security Data.

Oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and Suez Canal each increased while those through the Bab el-Mandeb decreased compared with the second quarter, when flows were severely constrained following the onset of the conflict with Iran.

Flows around the Middle East increased because of the use of smaller ships to move oil out of the Persian Gulf for ship-to-ship transfers of crude oil onto VLCCs, and producers have maximized utilization of infrastructure to bypass the areas of highest risk.
1Q25=first quarter of 2025 We estimate that countries around the Middle East produced 23.1 million barrels per day (b/d) of crude oil in October, the most since the beginning of the conflict.
Despite rising exports and more production, the Brent crude oil spot price averaged $124 per barrel (b) in October, the highest in any month since the conflict began.

items.title: China Oct alumina output retreats from record high; oversupply persists
points: China’s alumina output fell from a record high in October, but the domestic market remained under pressure from oversupply, as deteriorating refinery margins have yet to trigger widespread production cuts, market participants said.

China produced 8.12 million metric tons of alumina in October, down 3.3% month over month from a record 8.4 million mt in September, but 5.7% higher year over year, according to the latest data released by the National Bureau of Statistics Nov.
Average daily alumina output stood at 262,032 mt during the month, down 6.4% from September, according to calculations by Platts, part of S&P Global Energy.
China’s alumina output totaled 77.78 million mt over January-October, up 3.8% from the same period last year.
Output cuts limited Average losses across China’s alumina sector widened in October as prices declined, with around 90% of refineries operating at a loss, according to a Chinese analyst.

items.title: UBS flags resilient commodity investment case despite easing oil supply premium
points: UBS sees continued investment opportunities in critical minerals and power infrastructure as rising electricity demand, artificial intelligence spending, and electrification support long-term growth, even as technology-sector volatility raises concerns…

In a November 16 research note, UBS said structural demand for electricity and digital infrastructure remains a major investment theme, supporting opportunities across grid modernization, renewable energy, nuclear power and industrial automation.
The bank expects annual investment in power and related infrastructure to reach $3 trillion by 2030, driven partly by expanding data center capacity.
Data centers could account for approximately 9% of total U.S. electricity consumption by 2035, compared with around 4% currently, according to BloombergNEF forecasts cited by UBS.
This anticipated increase is expected to accelerate spending on electricity networks, generation capacity and critical minerals required for infrastructure development.
Still, substantial investment pipelines and strong order backlogs support its longer-term outlook for companies exposed to electrification and power demand.
UBS estimates overall AI-related capital expenditure will reach $1 trillion in 2026 before climbing to $1.4 trillion in 2027.

items.title: Metals sell-off runs ahead of physical markets
points: The speed of the sell-off looks more like a sharp repricing of investor exposure than a broad weakening in physical markets.
Copper has taken the biggest hit as investors unwind bullish positions and reassess AI-related demand.
Yet the sharp correction in prices contrasts with still-tight physical markets.
Investor selling weighs on copper Copper is on track for one of its steepest weekly declines in a decade.
Shanghai inventories are at their lowest since late 2023, while the Yangshan premium reached a record $500/t this week.
Bloomberg reports that some US copper is now being offered to buyers in China, where physical availability remains tight.
Gold feels the pressure from higher rates Gold has fallen for five straight sessions and is down around 9% this week, putting it on course for its steepest weekly decline since March.
Prices have also touched their lowest level since September 2025.

items.title: LME copper briefly falls below $12,000 a ton as tech selloff deepens
points: Copper prices briefly fell below $12,000 a ton on Monday, as mounting concerns over artificial intelligence spending, a stronger U.S. dollar and the prospect of higher interest rates weighed on investor sentiment.

Benchmark three-month Copper Futures on the London Metal Exchange fell to around $11,958.93 a ton during early trading, its weakest level since March, before recovering to $12,240.50, rising 1% by 03:40 GMT.
The metal had lost about 9% last week, its steepest weekly decline in more than 19 months.

The latest losses followed a broader selloff in technology shares, particularly companies linked to artificial intelligence, as investors questioned whether massive investments in data centres and related infrastructure would generate sufficient returns.
Copper, widely used in power grids, construction and data-centre infrastructure, had rallied earlier this year on expectations of strong AI-driven demand.

A stronger dollar and growing expectations of further Federal Reserve monetary tightening have added to the pressure, making dollar-priced commodities more expensive for buyers using other currencies.

items.title: Copper Prices Stabilize After Sharp Selloff
points: Copper futures steadied above $5.50 per pound on Monday following a steep decline last week, as investors continued to evaluate the outlook for artificial intelligence-driven demand.

Last week, the metal had fallen to its lowest level in more than seven months amid a broader unwinding of AI-related investments, with strong earnings from Nvidia and Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failing to revive market sentiment.
Copper remains a critical component of the global AI infrastructure buildout due to its extensive use in data centers and power networks.
Elsewhere, traders are preparing to redirect copper shipments from the massive stockpile accumulated in the US to help ease tightening supply conditions in China.

This represents a significant shift from the trend over the past two years, when traders increasingly routed copper to the US amid expectations that the Trump administration could impose import tariffs.

items.title: How the oil market could move from famine to glut
points: The constraint of Gulf crude exports since the closure of the Strait of Hormuz in March pushed Brent prices above US$100/bbl for much of the past nine months, triggering soaring fuel prices, rising inflation and weaker economic growth.
Senior VP Alan Gelder and the wider WoodMac Macro Oils team foresee the potential for much lower prices when flows of exports resume on a peace agreement, reversing these knock-on effects.
The key assumption in our new Base Case is that the US and Iran reach a peace agreement late in 2026, but with no breakthrough in the Russia-Ukraine war.
Crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz normalise progressively through 2027, allowing fundamentals to play a greater role in shaping the market once again.
Without a credible threat of attack, Iran waits out the rest of President Trump’s term.
Strait of Hormuz transits do not fully normalise until after 2028 and Middle East crude output stays around 3 million b/d below our Base Case through 2027-28.

points: US natural gas prices fell more than 7% to around $3.15 per million British thermal units on Monday, likely due to profit-taking after prices rose to an over nine-month high on Friday.
The recent rally was supported by forecasts of colder weather across the Midwest and Northeast this week, which could boost heating demand.
However, ample domestic supplies and comfortable storage levels continue to weigh on prices.

items.title: Arabian Drilling picks up $400m in long-term offshore work
points: Saudi Arabian drilling contractor Arabian Drilling has secured a SAR1.5bn ($400m) long-term contract from Khafji Joint Operations (KJO) to provide and operate two self-propelled offshore service units.
The first unit will operate under a 10-year contract, with work expected to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026.
The second has secured a 15-year agreement, with operations scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2028.
Arabian Drilling said the agreements represent the longest offshore service unit contracts in its history and will provide additional long-term revenue visibility.
The latest award takes the company’s cumulative contracted backlog to approximately SAR18.5bn ($4.9bn), a record for the Saudi contractor.
Khafji Joint Operations is a joint venture between Aramco Gulf Operations and Kuwait Gulf Oil, responsible for oil and gas production in the Saudi–Kuwaiti Divided Zone.
The contract follows Arabian Drilling’s September award of four high-specification offshore jackup contracts from KJO, worth approximately SAR2bn ($533m).

items.title: China says ready to work with India to facilitate visa issuance for business people

items.title: ‘The decade India turned the tide on poverty’
points: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman. | Photo Credit: ANI A year ago, during my visit to Kiphire, an aspirational district in the remote hills of Nagaland, I interacted with tribal women from local self-help groups.
Among them was Esther, a Lakhpati Didi, who proudly spoke of her millet-based products reaching customers online, far beyond Nagaland.
I encouraged them to dream bigger and become Crorepati Didis.

Their stories reflected a transformation reaching India’s remotest corners, where geographical and economic challenges have long constrained opportunities, yet aspirations for a better tomorrow are growing.
When the World Bank released its Poverty & Equity Brief on India last month, my interaction in Kiphire came back to me.
The report showed that nearly 50 crore Indians had moved out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, while extreme poverty has been almost eradicated.
Even in the early 2010s, India was portrayed abroad as a home of enduring destitution, lagging in sanitation, nutrition, clean cooking fuel and banking.

items.title: 'Lord Ram incomplete without Nepal': PM Modi, Balen Shah underline deep cultural, religious ties between nations
points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday said India shares deep cultural and religious ties with Nepal, asserting that Lord Ram was "incomplete" without the Himalayan nation, as he welcomed his Nepalese counterpart, Balen Shah, in New Delhi.
Addressing a joint press conference with Shah, PM Modi said the relationship between India and Nepal was built on shared history, faith and culture.

Prime Minister Modi also recalled his visit to the holy cities of Janakpur and Muktinath in May 2018, during a state visit where he and then-Nepal prime minister KP Sharma Oli flagged off the inaugural direct bus service between Janakpur and Ayodhya.
In 2018, on the sacred land of Janakpur, I had said that our pilgrimage sites are incomplete without Nepal, and our Lord Ram is incomplete without Nepal," he said.

items.title: 'Can't Be Pursued Through PIL': Supreme Court On UP Voter Roll Corrections Plea
points: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a PIL seeking corrections to municipal electoral rolls in Uttar Pradesh over discrepancies in house numbers.

"The right to seek correction of an electoral-roll entry is personal to the individual voter and cannot ordinarily be pursued collectively through a PIL.
